text: Paola Severino, born on 22 October 1948 in Naples, is an Italian lawyer, academic, and politician. She studied law at La Sapienza University of Rome and graduated in 1971. She began her career as a researcher at the Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (National Council of Research) in 1972, working there until 1975, after which she served as an assistant professor at La Sapienza from 1975 to 1987. She later worked at Perugia University, teaching penal commercial law at the Faculty of Economics. In 1997, she was appointed vice president of the Superior Council of Military Magistracy, becoming the first Italian woman to hold this position; her tenure lasted until 2002. She also worked with Giovanni Maria Flick, former President of the Italian Constitutional Court. Severino is recognized as one of Italy’s top criminal lawyers and has represented prominent clients such as former Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Cesare Geronzi, and Francesco Caltagirone in the Cirio trial, as well as the Italian energy giant Eni. She served as head of the law department at LUISS Guido Carli University from 2003 to 2006 and previously held positions as professor of penal law at the School for Carabinieri Officers and Pro-Rector Vicar at LUISS Guido Carli University. On 16 November 2011, she was appointed Minister of Justice in the Monti cabinet, becoming the first woman to hold this office in Italian history; her income in 2011 exceeded seven million euros, making her the highest-paid minister in the cabinet. Her term ended in April 2013, when Anna Maria Cancellieri succeeded her. She is married to former CONSOB executive Paolo Di Benedetto, with whom she has a daughter, and is an amputee who lost her right arm due to illness. On 3 October 2016, she was nominated rector of Libera Università Internazionale degli Studi Sociali Guido Carli. From 2018 to 2020, she served as Special Representative of the President-in-Office of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) for the fight against corruption, a role established by the Italian Presidency of the organization in 2018.
